name: tomcat-jvm-crash-log
why: a server JVM that crashes writes hs_err_pid<pid>.log in its working directory; the create is the crash trace the rule keys on
source: synthetic: Tomcat started from /opt/tomcat crashes; HotSpot names the file hs_err_pid<pid>.log in the working directory

name: jsvc-jvm-crash-log-in-tmp
why: a JVM hosted in jsvc (commons-daemon) whose working directory is not writable falls back to /tmp; the rule keys on the file, not on the java binary, so a JVM in another launcher still fires
source: synthetic: Tomcat under /usr/bin/jsvc crashes with a read-only working directory

name: trr9040-emulation-crash-log
why: TRR9040 Procedure A: a JVM whose OutOfMemoryError -XX:+CrashOnOutOfMemoryError makes fatal creates hs_err_pid<pid>.log in its working directory, the same file a SIGSEGV in C2-compiled code writes; this is the emulation's own record, so the rename test (R4) renames trr9040 and the rule must still fire
source: the shape detections/k8s/auditd_file_events.py writes for the runner's auditd dir watch on /tmp/trr9040-crash (a PATH item with nametype=CREATE under the key k8s_node_file); pid and timestamp illustrative

name: log-shipper-reads-crash-log
why: a log shipper that opens an existing crash log for reading shares the path but is not the crash; only the create fires
source: synthetic: a log agent reading /opt/tomcat/hs_err_pid48213.log after the crash

name: jvm-creates-gc-log
why: a running JVM creating its GC log is a .log create by the same process with no crash; only the hs_err_pid name separates them

name: logrotate-compresses-crash-log
why: compressing an old crash log creates hs_err_pid<pid>.log.gz; it shares the name but is housekeeping, not a new crash
source: synthetic: gzip run by logrotate on an old crash log

name: jvm-heap-dump
why: -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError writes java_pid<pid>.hprof; an out-of-memory dump is not a native crash and must not fire
source: synthetic: HotSpot heap dump on OutOfMemoryError
